lines.description: Research and development of multimodal models (VLMs) and Small Language Models (SLMs) applied to structured document parsing, complex layout reasoning, and neural OCR.
Investigation into semantic and instance segmentation, spatial-spectral representations (FFT), and foundational backbones (DINOv3).
Orchestration of distributed training and fine-tuning pipelines on multi-GPU clusters using Slurm and remote SSH, emphasizing scalability and reproducibility.

lines.area: Lightweight Models, Domain Adaptation & Edge AI
lines.description: Optimization for edge inference (quantization, autoencoders, Few-Shot Learning) and domain shift mitigation under data constraints.

projects.title: Face Forgery Detection under Realistic Degradation
projects.description: Undergraduate thesis that gave rise to the paper presented at SIBGRAPI 2026. A unified framework to evaluate robustness, cross-dataset generalization and explainability of deepfake detectors, comparing CNNs, Vision Transformers and the self-supervised DINOv3 model across spatial and spectral (2D-FFT) representations. We are continuing the research to publish a more robust version of the work.

projects.title: Document Understanding — ICDAR 2026 Challenges
projects.lab: Academic League of Artificial Intelligence — PUCPR
projects.description: We are currently researching Document Understanding at the AI League, continuing the ICDAR 2026 challenges: document comprehension with multimodal models (VLMs), layout analysis, OCR and structured information extraction. The League also takes part in other scientific competitions, such as the ICPR 2026 low-resolution license plate recognition challenge.

projects.title: Representation Fusion for Domain Adaptation of Deep Models in Intelligent Parking Space Monitoring
projects.description: Second undergraduate research grant. Applied research on representation fusion and domain adaptation for smart parking monitoring. Implementing and benchmarking Autoencoders (VAE, Denoising and deep variants), CNNs and federated models, with data augmentation pipelines to mitigate domain discrepancies and Podman containerization for reproducibility.

projects.title: Domain Adaptation in Deep Classification Models Applied to Parking Space Detection
projects.description: First undergraduate research grant (CNPq). Development of domain adaptation and few-shot learning methods for computer vision models applied to parking spot detection. Modeled CNNs, Autoencoders and classical classifiers, achieving results comparable to the literature even with small datasets. This parking research line led to the paper published at IEEE SMC 2026.

projects.title: Vision-Language Models & SLMs for Document Understanding
projects.description: Graduate courses and research at the Graduate Program in Computer Science (PPGIA/PUCPR) focusing on Vision-Language Models (VLMs), Small Language Models (SLMs), and comprehensive document understanding. Training and benchmarking multimodal models on High Performance Computing (HPC) clusters orchestrated via Slurm and operated over headless SSH, exploring structured extraction, neural OCR, and visual reasoning under computational constraints.

publications.title: Benchmarking Spatial, Spectral, and Self-Supervised Cues for Face Forgery Detection under Realistic Degradation
publications.abstract: Originated from my thesis: a robustness benchmark of convolutional, spectral (FFT) and self-supervised (DINOv3) representations for face forgery detection under realistic degradations.

publications.title: An Ensemble-Based Self-Taught Learning Approach for Parking Space Classification Under Limited Data
publications.abstract: Self-taught learning with an autoencoder ensemble for parking space classification under limited labels, reaching 93%–96% accuracy in cross-dataset evaluation.
